sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and the Diagnostic Pitfall: When Neck Swelling is Not Angioedema
sections.description: This section analyzes the initial patient presentation, focusing on why the case was initially misdiagnosed as an infectious or allergic process. It details the specific clinical features that should raise suspicion for an underlying myopathy despite the dominant appearance of soft tissue edema.
subtopics: Differentiating inflammatory neck edema from Ludwig's angina and deep neck space infections
Clinical criteria distinguishing histaminergic/bradykinin-mediated angioedema from pseudoangioedema
Identifying subtle cutaneous clues: Periungual telangiectasias, Holster sign, and facial erythema
The significance of concurrent proximal muscle weakness and dysphagia in the context of neck swelling
Initial laboratory red flags: Disproportionately elevated CK, AST/ALT, and LDH

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology and Serology: Understanding Anti-SAE1 Dermatomyositis
sections.description: This section provides the necessary background on Dermatomyositis (DM) with a specific focus on the rare anti-SAE1 antibody subtype. It explains the molecular mechanism of sumoylation, the unique clinical phenotype associated with this antibody, and the pathological basis for the 'pseudoangioedema' presentation.
subtopics: Overview of Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies and the bimodal age distribution
Mechanism of action: The role of Small Ubiquitin-like Modifier Activating Enzyme (SAE1) and sumoylation
Characteristic clinical phenotype of anti-SAE1 DM: High prevalence of dysphagia and interstitial lung disease
Pathogenesis of subcutaneous edema in DM: Complement-mediated microangiopathy vs. true angioedema
Epidemiology of edema as a presenting symptom in dermatomyositis cohorts

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Workup and Reasoning: From Bedside to Biopsy
sections.description: This section outlines the step-by-step diagnostic algorithm used to confirm the diagnosis. It emphasizes the hierarchy of testing, from ruling out common causes to utilizing advanced serology, imaging, and histopathology to secure a definitive diagnosis.
subtopics: Exclusionary workup: Normal complement levels (C3/C4) and C1-esterase inhibitor function
Interpretation of Autoimmune panels: ANA patterns and specific myositis antibody arrays
Imaging modalities: Utility of MRI for muscle inflammation vs. PET-CT for metabolic activity and malignancy screening
Histopathological hallmarks: Perifascicular atrophy, perimysial inflammation, and C5b-9 membrane attack complex deposition
Assessing visceral involvement: Video fluoroscopic swallow studies and pulmonary function tests

sections.section_title: Therapeutic Strategy and Malignancy Surveillance in High-Risk Myositis
sections.description: This section details the management principles for severe, antibody-defined dermatomyositis. It covers aggressive induction therapy, steroid-sparing strategies tailored to organ involvement, prophylactic care, and the rigorous cancer screening protocols mandated by international guidelines for high-risk patients.
subtopics: Induction therapy protocols: High-dose intravenous corticosteroids and IVIG loading doses
Selection of steroid-sparing agents: Rationale for choosing Mycophenolate Mofetil over Methotrexate in lung-involved disease
Role of Rituximab in refractory or severe antibody-positive dermatomyositis
Infection prophylaxis during intense immunosuppression (PJP prevention)
Malignancy risk stratification using IMACS guidelines: Integrating antibody status, demographics, and clinical features
Comprehensive cancer screening algorithms: Imaging, tumor markers, and endoscopic surveillance
